articles.summary: Agents read text written by strangers as part of normal work. You cannot reliably filter out every instruction, so limit what an agent can do after it reads one.
articles.title: The prompt injection hiding in your tickets and emails

articles.summary: Every agent stops on some share of its work. Decide where that work goes, who picks it up, and what context comes with it, so nobody has to start over.
articles.title: Where should work go when an AI agent gets stuck?

articles.summary: An agent can act on behalf of a person or under a dedicated agent identity. Choose per job, keep the person as the ceiling, and record both names on every action.
articles.title: Whose permissions does an AI agent act with?

articles.summary: Most AI policies are long, vague, and unread. One page that says which agents are approved, what they may do, who stays accountable, and how to report a problem does more.
articles.title: How to write an AI agent policy your employees will read

articles.summary: How Protoguard detects prompt injection in MCP traffic out of band, why we monitor instead of blocking inline, and where it still falls short.
